about: We collect railway vehicle classes (groups of vehicles built to the same design) from Wikidata and other authorities. Japanese classes are not included.
The 3D models are bodies designed to fit a toy chassis. They are not scale models. Each model is linked to the class and livery it depicts.

dataset.title: Dataset
dataset.description: About the RailClass dataset: counts, dump files, URI pattern, licences, no SPARQL endpoint, sources.
dataset.lead: RailClass publishes {classes} railway vehicle classes from outside Japan as Linked Data, linked to Wikidata. This page puts the counts, files, URIs, licences and sources in one place. The same description is also available for machines (VoID and DCAT).

classes: {exactMatch} linked to their Wikidata items with skos:exactMatch; the rest are classes of our own with no Wikidata item
photo: foaf:depiction, with the same Wikimedia Commons IRI as Wikidata P18
values: Operator, manufacturer, country, gauge and more, kept as Wikidata IRIs
lines: {lines} lines; {withLineShape} classes and {lineShapes} lines have an OpenStreetMap track on the map
models: Linked to {withModel} classes; {liveries} liveries, {iiifManifests} IIIF Manifests
eratv: Types in the European Register of Authorised Types of Vehicles (ERATV) matched to {eratvClasses} Wikidata classes

dataset.filesLead: The dump holds every class, every 3D model and our own terms. Start with all.ttl.

files.lines: Line tracks (GeoJSON; one file per line at lines/<Q id>.geojson)

dataset.uriTitle: URIs and how to get the data
uri: A class is {cls}<ID> and a 3D model is {mdl}<ID>. <ID> is the Wikidata Q id (e.g. Q696668), or an ID of our own starting with tb- for the few classes Wikidata has no item for.

The URIs are persistent w3id.org URIs: they stay the same if the site moves. Opening one in a browser shows a page for people; asking with Accept: text/turtle or application/ld+json gives the RDF (w3id.org sends the request on to the file).
The files are also at {site}: the URI's page with .ttl or .jsonld in place of .html (for example {site}rdf/class/Q696668.ttl).
sparql: There is no SPARQL endpoint. The site is static files only.
To query the data, load all.ttl into a local triple store (Oxigraph, Apache Jena, ...) or rdflib. It is {triples} triples ({allTtlSize} of Turtle) and loads in seconds on a laptop.
To look at one resource, open its URI in LD Browser, a Linked Data browser that runs in the browser alone.

sources: Classes and their values: Wikidata. The items that are railway vehicle classes were collected with SPARQL; Japanese classes are left out.
Lines: Wikidata P3438 (vehicle normally used), and a hand-filled table with sources. The tracks were cut out of OpenStreetMap.
ERATV mapping: the ERATV type list matched to Wikidata classes by name, automatically. Not checked by hand.
3D models: vehicle bodies made for 3D printing, sized for a toy chassis (not scale models).
